messages.content: Predict a real participant's contribution in one of five one-shot allocation scenarios displayed together on a single screen. Each scenario gives you its own 20-point budget: choose x from 0 to 20 to put in a group project, keeping20-x. You and two other participants form a three-person group; group matching and outcome feedback occur after all survey questions. In a scenario, X is the sum of all three contributions. Each project point generates 2.5 total benefit points. A fraction alpha of these benefits goes to the Make-a-Wish Foundation, a charity fulfilling wishes for children with critical illnesses; the remaining fraction is divided equally among the three participants. Your payoff is 20-x+(1-alpha)*(5/6)*X; each other member gets their own retained points plus the same project return. Make-a-Wish receives(5/2)*alpha*X points. Thus alpha0 is a PGG with no charity benefit; alpha1 gives all project benefits to charity and no project return to group members; intermediate values blend the two. You do not know others' contributions. There is no repeated-game reciprocity or interim outcome feedback. All five scenarios appear together in randomized visual order, but each is an independent one-shot 20-point decision. Only one alpha is randomly selected for the entire group and its outcome is used for experimental payment; do not add five budgets or payoffs into one paid portfolio. Current co-visible answer entries and actual entry order are unavailable, so no other same-form response is supplied as earlier history. Point-to-GBP conversion is unavailable here; points are not pounds. Before choosing, participants answered control questions and received explanations for errors; original item-level responses are unavailable. Predict the human contribution without advice or reasons. Output only the recorded number of points contributed to the current project, between 0 and 20.

Current target scenario: alpha=0. Available budget: 20 points. All five co-visible alphas, in source visual order: [0,0.25,1,0.5,0.75]. The current scenario is at visual position 1/5; this is not a chronological round. Participation fee for this cohort: 2.5 GBP; separate from these point allocations.
Own stable background: age 20 years; male

Predict a real participant's current charity allocation. You have 20 points and can donate g from 0 to 20 to your preferred charity. You retain 20-g points. Regardless of your own contribution, the charity is guaranteed a total of 20 points: the experimenter adds the difference 20-g. Your contribution therefore replaces experimenter funding one-for-one rather than increasing the charity's total. Choose for the current opportunity based only on these rules. The charity is self-selected from Oxfam, Red Cross, Save the Children, WWF and Doctors without Borders. The specific charity identity is not supplied here. The point-to-money conversion is unavailable. Predict the native human answer without explanations or advice. Output only the number of own points donated, from 0 to 20.

Predict a real participant's additional donation to the same self-selected charity. An earlier allocation gave you 20 points; you donated g1 and retained20-g1. The experimenter topped up that earlier donation so the charity received20 points in total. You have now been offered an additional, previously unannounced opportunity to donate g2 from your remaining 20-g1 points. There is no further experimenter top-up or crowding out. The charity receives 20+g2 in total, while you retain 20-g1-g2. This is not a fresh20-point endowment. The earlier own donation and selected charity are supplied below; no later response, inferred motive type or final experimental outcome is an input. Point-to-money conversion is unavailable. Predict the actual human answer without reasons or advice. Output only the extra points donated, from 0 up to the current remaining balance.
